hints.title: Pair Search Obstacle
hints.text: Checking every pair costs O(N^2). When you reach an element, what would make it part of a valid pair, and what would you need to have remembered to know that immediately?

hints.title: Complement Lookup with Hash Map
hints.text: Store visited values alongside their array indices in a hash map. This allows you to check whether the required counterpart for the current number has already appeared in constant expected time.

hints.title: Single-Pass Traversal and Storage
hints.text: Iterate through the array while maintaining a map from number to index. For each number x at index i, calculate target - x. If that difference exists in the map, return the stored index and i. Otherwise, record x at index i in the map and continue.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: length of nums array (2 <= N <= 10^4)
complexity.notes: Single pass over nums with O(1) average hash table lookups and insertions.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Checking every pair costs O(N^2) time. For N = 10^4, this requires up to (10^4 * (10^4 - 1)) / 2 = ~5 * 10^7 operations, which is too slow and approaches the 1-second timeout limit on large arrays, while missing the hash map invariant.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Trading O(N) auxiliary space in a hash map to store previously seen numbers reduces time from O(N^2) brute force to O(N) single-pass lookup.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Immediate identification of the one-pass complement lookup, handling duplicate numbers correctly (e.g. [3, 3] target 6), returning indices rather than values, and avoiding using the same element twice.
